_doc: Fortified lines at each start date. Applied when a war breaks out: provinces of `fortify` that border provinces held by the other country get `level` (0..0.6; 0.6 = deep, multi-belt works, QJM's 'fortified' posture x1.6). A line listed with `provinces` applies only to those provinces (the 2015-2022 Donbas line, not the quiet Crimean boundary). Everywhere else fronts start unfortified and dig in while static (FORTIFICATION_GROWTH in conflict/land_warfare.py). Levels are judgement; each entry states its basis.

2021.basis: 2015-2022 Donbas line of contact, fortified by both sides for seven years (Avdiivka and Marinka held until 2024 and 2023). Ukraine's borders with Russia, Belarus and Crimea were not fortified before 24 February 2022.
Korean Demilitarized Zone: 248 km, mined and fortified in depth by both sides since 1953.
Line of Control in Kashmir, fenced and fortified (India's LoC fence completed 2004); fenced international border.
Line of Actual Control: permanent positions and roads built by both sides after the 2020 Galwan clash.
Israel's fortified northern border (barrier and strongpoints along the Blue Line).
Golan Heights defences on the 1974 disengagement line.
Contact line after the November 2020 ceasefire, with Russian peacekeepers in Nagorno-Karabakh.

2026.basis: A front static since late 2022: Russia's Surovikin line (built Oct 2022 - spring 2023), Ukraine's fortification belts (2024-2025), and fortified border regions on both sides after the 2024 Kursk incursion. CSIS (2025): Russian advances of 15-70 m/day, slower than the Somme.
Ukraine mined and fortified its border with Belarus after the 2022 offensive on Kyiv came through it.
Korean Demilitarized Zone (as 2021); North Korea added walls and mines on its side in 2024.
Line of Control and fenced border (as 2021); fighting in May 2025.
